AfterCardChangedPiles.maps_to: after_card_added_to_deck (darkstone_periapt.py:20-23), dispatched from run.add_card (run.py:352-353). The sim narrows C#'s generic pile-change event to the one case the relic cares about, so C#'s `card.Pile.Type == PileType.Deck` clause is structural in the sim and the `clonedBy` parameter has no counterpart (nothing in the sim tracks a cloner).
AfterCardChangedPiles.issue: Rollup of guards G1 (LIVE) and G2 per binding rule 4. The narrowing is only sound if every C# path that puts a card into PileType.Deck reaches run.add_card. It does not: the out-of-combat TRANSFORM path writes the deck directly.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): a Curse produced by an out-of-combat TRANSFORM pays the +6 Max HP in C# and nothing in the sim, because RunState.transform_card writes the deck list directly instead of going through add_card
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardCmd's transform loop fires BOTH deck hooks for the replacement when the pile is the deck -- Hook.ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck at CardCmd.cs:429 and Hook.AfterCardChangedPiles at CardCmd.cs:447 -- so DarkstonePeriapt.cs:16-24 sees the new card and grants MaxHpVar(6). RunState.transform_card (run.py:406-470) removes the original and does `self.deck.append(into)` (run.py:466) or `self.deck[idx] = into` (run.py:469) with no hook dispatch of any kind. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py darkstone): with the relic on the run, run.add_card(make_card('regret')) takes Max HP 80 -> 86 (correct), and then transform_card on that curse yields another curse ('clumsy') with Max HP staying at 86 where C# gives 92 -- observed 'DIVERGENCE: sim +0, C# +6'. Both sides are ported content: Darkstone Periapt is granted by the Trash Heap event (events/trash_heap.py:15), and a curse always transforms into another curse because run.py:440-441 switches the pool to CURSE_POOL for a CardType.CURSE original -- the same fact audit/records/relic/astrolabe.json G1 established for its own gap. Fifteen ported call sites reach transform_card, including relic/astrolabe (Darv shrine, transforms deck cards), relic/pandoras_box, relic/leafy_poultice, relic/new_leaf and six events (aroma_of_chaos, endless_conveyor, morphic_grove, symbiote, trial, whispering_hollow). The gap is not Periapt-specific -- the same missing dispatch silently disables relic/book_of_five_rings and relic/lucky_fysh on the transform path and skips the egg relics' ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck -- but the Periapt is where it is observable as a wrong Max HP, which DETECTOR 3's act-boundary HP assertion checks. RULE 7: this rationale leans on run.py, cards/pool.py and CardCmd.cs, none of which this record hashes.

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# fires AfterCardChangedPiles for a card entering PileType.Deck at ANY time, including mid-combat; the sim's after_card_added_to_deck exists only on the out-of-combat RunState.add_card path
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardPileCmd.cs:635 and :683 dispatch the hook from the general Add path, and PileType.Deck is a non-combat pile (CardPile.cs:29 IsCombatPile), so a card added to the run's deck while a fight is in progress still triggers it. The sim's CombatState works on a deep copy of the deck (run.create_combat) and nothing inside combat calls run.add_card, so a mid-combat deck add cannot reach the relic. DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is named: no ported card, power, potion or relic adds a card to the RUN's deck from inside a combat -- the in-combat generators all target combat piles via CardPileCmd.add_to_hand / the draw and discard piles. Porting any effect that adds a Curse to the deck mid-fight (the C# shape is CardPileCmd.AddCurseToDeck called from a monster power) makes it live.
